notes: The competing reading takes *So is* as one supplied run; the copula is licensed by the verbless construction (rule 20) and so joins the predicate nominal נֶזֶם, leaving only *So* `added` under rule 14's closing sentences. The Hebrew, not the English order, decides which side is the predicate — the comparison phrase predicates of the woman.
The rectum חֲזִיר is written as an English possessive, so the phrase's *a* stands before the possessor's word and goes with it under rule 29.

סָרַת takes *is without* because the participle's own lexeme is what *without* writes (rule 19's rider on a construct that is itself relational); the margin's 'turneth aside from' was read and set aside under rule 38.
